newsitem.title: USA: Leasing Solutions sees near-term hurt by Dell deal.
newsitem.headline: Leasing Solutions sees near-term hurt by Dell deal.

text.p: Leasing Solutions Inc said Monday that its near-term growth will be hurt by Dell Computer Corp's decision to form an affiliate leasing company with Newcourt Credit Group Inc of Toronto.

Earlier on Monday, Dell and Newcourt said they formed Dell Financial Services LP (DFS) as a joint venture to offer a wide range of leasing and asset management services to Dell's customers in the United States and eventually worldwide.
Shares of Leasing Solutions dropped 50 percent or 8-13/16 to 8-13/16.

"Dell's decision to form an affiliate leasing company will obviously have an impact on our near-term growth. Notwithstanding Dell's decision to form an affiliate leasing company, we expect our overall growth to continue at impressive rates as a result of other more recently announced vendor programs, other new sources of significant equipment volume, the company's geographic expansion into Europe and our anticipated near-term expansion to Canada," said Hal Krauter, Leasing Solution's chief executive.
Leasing Solution did not specify the extent Dell's venture will hurt its results, but the company said it expects to exceed analysts' estimates for 1997.
On a consensus basis, analysts expect Leasing Solutions to earn $1.48 a share in 1997, compared to earnings of $1.16 a share in 1996, according to First Call.

Despite Dell's new venture, Leasing Solution said it will serve a "recommended alternative" source of lease financing for Dell's corporate customers who choose to lease equipment from an independent leasing company.
Leasing Solutions also said it reached an agreement with Dell regarding the sale of Leasing Solution's existing domestic lease portfolio of Dell computer equipment to Dell Financial Services.
Exact terms of the deal were not provided, but Leasing Solutions said the original purchase price of the equipment in the portfolio was about $240 million.
The sale of the leasing portfolio is expected to occur from April 30, 1997, through March 31, 1998.
"The sale will provide significant financial and operational benefits to both companies," Leasing Solutions said.
"We see the transaction having a favorable impact for our shareholders," said Leasing Solutions' chief financial officer Steven Yeffa.

Leasing Solutions, which has been working with Dell for about two years, said it will elaborate about the impact of the Dell deal when it files its 8-K report with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The filing its expected to occur within the next 10 days, Yeffa said.
The company expects to retain a "modicum" of business related to Dell due to the excellant relationship between the two companies, Yeffa said.
The move by Dell to create the leasing and asset management services venture comes amid increasing concern throughout the computer industry about the cost of owning personal computers.

International Business Machines Corp also is expected to announce a major initiative Monday aimed at lowering the cost of owning, maintaining and upgrading personal computers for its corporate customers.

IBM plans to offer a one-stop shopping package so customers can lease PC hardware for a monthly fee that will cover financing, service, maintenance, support and upgrades, sources close to IBM told Reuters.
